title: web console UI grid not showing results
body:
### Describe the bug

simply as per title, any query on the editor show the number of columns of the result but the grid in the UI is always empty.

Apparently the component has been updated in [3068](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/3068)

### To reproduce

open web console UI
write a "select * from tableName"
the grid shows no results

the javascript of the UI fails with:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'digest')
    at qdb.js:2:913132
    at qdb.js:2:913264
    at qdb.js:2:913268
```


### Expected Behavior

the table should show result

### Environment

```markdown
- **QuestDB version**: 7.1
- **OS**: Any
- **Browser**: Any
```


### Additional context

_No response_

comments.body: This version is deployed on <redacted-host>. Can you check if queries work there on your browser. Please narrow down the browser

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I would love to fix the bug if only I could reproduce it

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
It could be the case that your browser doesn't support `crypto` Web API. If so, using another browser might help. This page lists the browsers: https://caniuse.com/?search=crypto

To support such browsers we could use a polyfill library (if any - I didn't check) or check the presence of `crypto` global and, if it's missing, use an alternative code path.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Same here. Pulled latest docker image to upgrade, and then query results don’t show up anymore.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
@participant1 crypto-api is usable only in a "secure context": https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CryptoKey

which means, any local installation which is not operated behind a https-proxy or the like will face the issue.

i have tested with safari, firefox, google-chrome against http://localhost:9000: all the same result of what @reporter reported.
https://<redacted-host> works like a charm.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hello, tried the demo at https://<redacted-host>/ and I can correctly view the results in the UI grid with Chrome Version 111.0.5563.147 (Official Build) (64-bit), I also can see the results on my mobile phone.
At this point I think it is not browser related as I tried with both my mobile phone and Chrome browser on the PC and the result are the same: the results in the UI grid are not shown.
I don't think it is related with the antivirus either otherwise the phone would work, I tried exporting the schema of the example tables in <redacted-host> and using them on our server and the result is the same, no results in the UI grid, so it is not related to the specific schema of our tables.
The only evidence something is gone awry is the debugger tools output:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'digest')
    at qdb.js:2:913132
    at qdb.js:2:913264
    at qdb.js:2:913268
:9000/exec?limit=0%2C1000&explain=true&count=true&src=con&query=SHOW%20CREATE%20TABLE%20rsrut1&timings=true:1          Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400 (Bad request)
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> @participant1 crypto-api is usable only in a "secure context": https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CryptoKey
> 
> which means, any local installation which is not operated behind a https-proxy or the like will face the issue.
> 
> i have tested with safari, firefox, google-chrome against http://localhost:9000: all the same result of what @reporter reported. https://<redacted-host> works like a charm.

In our deployment, we have always operated QuestDB without the use of certificates since both the QuestDB server and client run within our network, allowing for local data flow without being exposed to the outside. We believed that disabling TLS encryption could potentially remove a possible failure point and improve performance, thus we have kept it cleartext. Previously, this setup had worked without any issues up to version 7.1, which exhibited the problem described above. Therefore, we recommend either resolving the problem or explicitly stating that local connections without certificates cause issues with the web UI (in most browsers given that two random browsers exhibit the same behaviour).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Looks like the issue stands true when Web Console is accessed over plain HTTP (no SSL/TLS) and URL other than `127.0.0.1:port` or `localhost:port` (these two are considered an exception in the "secure context" requirement).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: As a fix, we should consider using alternative implementations in insecure contexts like https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge#sha256 or https://github.com/bitwiseshiftleft/sjcl/

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> As a fix, we should consider using alternative implementations in insecure contexts like https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge#sha256 or https://github.com/bitwiseshiftleft/sjcl/

Still not clear to me why the behaviour was different in 7.0.1 and we had this regression in 7.1. Using the same implementation as in 7.0.1 is possible?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> Still not clear to me why the behaviour was different in 7.0.1 and we had this regression in 7.1.

7.1 has improved grid features, so that's why we only have this issue in 7.1. As a temporary workaround, you could downgrade to 7.0.1. Alternatively, you can try running a local HTTP proxy, so that Web Console's URL is `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
@participant2 if the "new" behaviour is clearly documented, i do not see that much of an issue or a hard requirement to introduce additional deps. i have now slapped traefik in front of questdb to provide tls. operation within k8s and port-forwarding allows that `localhost` situation … if one is aware of that.

an improvement i do see is to catch the js-error itself and slap a warning into the face of the user to instantly have clear expectation management at work =)
